rationale: Kaarel's work on zero-shot ML matching problems and AI agents at Known.com directly complements Nathan's research into embodied AI and physics-informed learning at Afore and Extropic — both are pushing ML beyond traditional supervised paradigms. Kaarel's conviction that matching problems are solvable with modern ML pairs well with Nathan's focus on probabilistic methods and real-world grounding, and both have deep robotics backgrounds (Kaarel shipped Boston Dynamics infra, Nathan co-founded Extropic on physical embodiment). This is a mutual match where both could explore how embodied systems and next-gen matching apply to consumer AI.
intro_message: Kaarel Kaarelson, meet Nathan Yu — you're both shipping at the intersection of ML research and embodied systems, and your convictions on probabilistic methods and real-world grounding could unlock new approaches to the matching problems Kaarel is solving at Known.com.
